key_insight: KANs can accurately predict airfoil surface pressure and interpolate across Mach number and angle of attack, but they do not clearly outperform a well-tuned MLP and are outperformed by a GNN in this study.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs offer a potentially lower-complexity and faster-training alternative, but they require careful tuning and do not yet displace strong baseline architectures.
method: Compare KANs against MLPs and GNNs on pressure-coefficient prediction for subsonic and transonic airfoils.
Evaluate interpolation capability across Mach numbers and angles of attack.
Assess accuracy, model complexity, and training cost/training stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KANs perform well on full pressure-coefficient prediction and interpolation, but are marginally inferior to the best MLP and below the best GNN, which achieves top accuracy at longer training cost.
watch_item: KAN performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameter optimization and can suffer from training instabilities.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
